attack_indicators: presence of suspicious or obfuscated URLs in email body
use of urgent or enticing subject lines related to health, finance, or job offers
inclusion of misspellings, grammatical errors, and nonsensical filler text to evade detection
attack_signatures: phishing emails often contain calls to action urging users to click links or provide personal information, e.g., 'Click Here!', 'Guaranteed results', 'Update your payment information'
use of brand impersonation or spoofed reputable sources, e.g., fake CNN newsletter style with embedded URLs
insertion of random or nonsensical word sequences (e.g., 'epicranium excellente ethylhexyl') to confuse text-based filters
technical_markers: URL presence rate: >1 suspicious URL per email body often indicates phishing
high frequency of health or medication-related keywords in phishing samples (e.g., 'Viagra', 'medications', 'herbal breakthrough')
subject line length typically short and generic or overly promotional (e.g., 'Job Vacancies', 'Guaranteed Erection Fast')
normal_indicators: benign emails contain technical, professional, or community discussion content without urgent calls to action
subjects are descriptive and relevant to the email body content, e.g., mailing list discussions, technical problem reports
email bodies have coherent, well-structured text with minimal spelling or grammatical errors
baseline_metrics: average URL count per email body close to zero or only legitimate URLs
absence of suspicious keywords related to health products, financial urgency, or job offers
subject line length moderate, typically descriptive and specific (e.g., '[Python-Dev] GSoC student introduction')
